question.text: A Nifty call option with strike 17,500 trades at Rs. 310. Above what level does the call buyer start making profit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Call breakeven point = Strike + Premium = 17,500 + 310 = Rs. 17,810. Above 17,810 the call buyer's intrinsic value (Spot - Strike) exceeds the Rs. 310 premium paid, so profit becomes positive. The Trap: Profit starts above the breakeven point, not above the strike. Between the strike (Rs. 17,500) and the breakeven (Rs. 17,810) the call has positive intrinsic value but the buyer is only recovering part of the premium and is still net negative. Note: The duplicate Rs. 17,810 distractor was replaced with Rs. 18,120 so the four options now contain exactly one correct answer. The unsupported Cross-Exam Context and Pro-Tip paragraphs were removed.
